summary: Configured persistent daily rotation for /var/log/inventory/app.log, retaining seven compressed rotations. Verified an open writer continues writing via copytruncate, then rebooted node1 and confirmed the configuration, timer, and log data recovered under a new boot identity.
actions_performed: Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory with daily, rotate 7, compress, missingok, notifempty, and copytruncate.
Validated the configuration with logrotate debug parsing.
Forced a live rotation while holding the log file open; verified compressed retained data and a successful post-rotation write through the same descriptor.
Restarted node1 exactly once and verified recovery.

evidence.requirement: Rotate app.log daily and retain seven compressed rotations
evidence.summary: Shows the installed rule, successful parsing, active daily timer, next scheduled run, and persistence after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Allow continued application writes after rotation
evidence.summary: The inode remained unchanged across forced rotation, pre-rotation data appeared in app.log.1.gz, and a post-rotation write appeared in the active log.

Captures healthy baseline boot ID 54089086-53d1-408b-a22f-57b1dea70e03, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID e5806a89-6611-4dc6-905a-2b21569888d0, and recovered timer, configuration, active log, and compressed data.
